caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 628 of 2011
lawyer:
Qumrul Haque Siddique, Advocate instructed byNurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Mahmudul lslam, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar 	Rahman, Advocate-on-Record -----For Respondent No.1.
M Khaled Ahmed, Advocate instructed by Aziz Toufique, Advocate-on-Record -----For Respondent No.3.
parties:
Abdul Malek (Md) ------ Petitioner
VS
Md Asaduzzman Belal and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that respondent No. 3 herein, Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Tongi Branch, Tongi, Gazipur (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) instituted Artha Rin SuitNo, 36 of 2004 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Gazipur for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 34,65,698 as well as interest thereon till realization thereof impleading the petitioner herein and respondent No.4, M/s Hossain and sons poultry as defendants. Eventually, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 9-8-2004. The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal dues, the decree-holder- Bank levied Artha Jari Case No. 52.of 2004 on 20-11-2004 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur (hereinafter referred to as the executing Court) for recovery of the decretal dues. In the arthajari case, notice was published in the daily newspaper for auction sale of the mortgaged property of the judgment-debtors. 3(three) bidders participated in the auction held on 4-6-2006 and Md Asaduzzaman Belal became the highest bidder offering Taka 12,01,000. The offer was not accepted by the Executing Court and the auction was cancelled. Thereafter, the second auction was held on 7-8-2005. Again three bidders including Md Asaduzzaman Belal participated in the auction and Md Asaduzzaman Belal became the highest bidder at Taka 12,10,000 and this time, the bid was accepted on 14-8-2005. The auction-purchaser deposited the entire auction money and sale certificate was issued in his favour on 27-9-2005. Thereafter the mortgaged land was duly registered in favour of the auction-purchaser by the Executing Court in the Office of the Sub-Registrar. At this stage, the full brother of judgment-debtor No. 2 (the petitioner herein) as 3rd party claimant filed an application before the Executing Court under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code). The said application was rejected on 7-2-2006 against which the brother of the judgment-debtor filed Civil Revision No. 8 of 2005 which was subsequently rejected on 22-1-2008, though application was filed to withdraw the civil revision. On 26-5-2008, judgment-debtor No. 2 (hereinafter referred to as the judgment-debtor) filed an application before the Executing Court under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, 2003) by depositing Taka 6,65,500 with 10% profit (in the application in Bengali, it has been written as ১০%লভ্যাংশfor setting aside the auction sale and the bainama and to pass necessary order to return the mortgaged property to him stating, inter alia, that he had no homestead except the mortgaged property sold in auction. He had been in South Korea for which he could not pay the loan to the Bank and the decree was obtained through fraudulent means. The Executing Court by the order dated 29-7-2008 cancelled the auction sale dated 7-8-2005, the acceptance order dated 14-8-2005 and the sale certificate issued on 27-9-2005. By the same order, the Executing Court also directed that the auction purchaser would get 10% interest from 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 amounting to Taka 3,63,000 along with bid money of Taka 12,10,000 and other costs of Taka 70,000, i.e. in total Taka 16,43,000 and directed the judgment-debtor to deposit the money within 30 (thirty) days from date, failing which "the order shall. stand dismissed." Challenging this order, the auction purchaser filed the writ petition on the ground that he was a bonafide purchaser, sale certificate was duly issued in his favour and it was also duly registered in the Office of the Sub-Registrar through the Court and so, there was no scope for cancellation of auction sale and a registered sale certificate on an application filed by the judgment-debtor under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 long after 3 (three ) years of the auction sale. 

 4. The judgment-debtor as writ-respondent No. 3 (hereinafter referred to as the judgment-debtor) contested the Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that as per the order of the Executing Court, he paid the principal amount of loan and prayed for remission of interest which was pending for decision in view of the pendency of the instant writ petition. The decree was passed ex-parte in favour of the Bank without the knowledge of the judgment-debtor while he was abroad. The judgment-debtor came to know about the ex-parte decree and the auction sale after coming back from abroad and deposited the auction money along with 10% profit of the auction price. Therefore, the Executing Court by the impugned order rightly cancelled the auction sale considering that the homestead of the judgment-debtor is situated in the auction sold land and that he has no other land to live in. As the entire decretal amount had been paid and the execution case was disposed of with full satisfaction on 7-9-2008, the Rule Nisi was liable to be discharged. 

 10. Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing for the judgment-debtor-petitioner, has submitted that the Executing Court considering the facts, namely: (a) the auction purchaser submitted the bids collusively showing him as the highest bidder in both the auction sale (first auction was held on 14-6-2005, that auction was not accepted, second auction was held on 7-8-2005), (b) the judgment-debtor took a loan of taka 16,14,000 on 13-4-1995 mortgaging the auction sold land (in the impugned order dated 27-7-2008, it has been wrongly mentioned as the suit land) and naturally, it could not be said that value of the auction sold land on 13- 4-1995 was not less than Taka 16,14,000. So sale of the auction sold land on 7-8-2005, i.e. after 10(ten) years at taka 12,10,000 was "definitely not a market price" (c) the petitioner asserted in his application that the present value of the auction sold land was more than Taka 40,00,000 (Forty Lakh) and that he would pay the entire loan money along with interest and expenses, (d) besides, the petitioner stated that there is homestead in the auction sold land and except this land he has no land to live in, came to the finding that there was material irregularity in conducting the sale which caused substantial injury to the judgment-debtor-applicant and such injury was the result of fraud, but the High Court Division in setting aside the order of the Executing Court did not at all consider the said findings of the Executing Court. He has submitted that in setting aside the auction sale, the Executing Court took notice of the fact that from the copy of the passport it appeared that during the whole period judgment-debtor was in South Korea, the Executing Court also passed order directing the judgment-debtor to deposit the entire bid money of Taka 12,10,000 along with 10% interest from 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 amounting to Taka 3,63,000 and other costs of Taka 70,000, i.e. in total Taka 16,43,000 and pursuant to the said direction, he already deposited the said amount which has been clearly noted in the next order being No. 41 dated 28-8-2008 and the Bank had already withdrawn the auction money of Taka 12,10,000 and accordingly, the execution case was disposed of as being fully satisfied and in view of the fact that the auction purchaser had been sufficiently compensated by the Executing Court by giving him interest at the rate of 10% from 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 and the other incidental costs, he Could not have any grievance to maintain the writ petition. Mr Siddique has submit- ted that during the pendency of the writ petition at the verbal order of the Court (the High Court Division), the judgment-debtor deposited the entire dues of the Bank amounting to Taka 36,35,550 vide receipts dated 26-1-2011 and 31-1-2011 and the Bank having received the entire dues applied to the Executing Court to dispose of the execution case as being withdrawn (প্রত্যাহারমূলে), as it would not proceed with the same and accordingly, the Executing Court by order dated 12-9-2011 disposed of the execution case as being fully satisfied. In this regard, he has also referred to the certificate issued by the Assistant-General Manager of the Bank issued on 20-7-2011 filed with the additional paper book wherein it has been stated that there was no dues of the Bank against the judgment-debtor. Mr Siddique has submitted that the Executing Court had inherent power to recall orders obtained by practising fraud on It at the instance of a party to the proceedings and in case of fraud, there is no question of the Court being functus-officio; a party cannot be allowed to take advantage of its own wrong as fraud vitiates everything, but the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering that established principle of law which has occasioned failure of justice. He has submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the mortgaged property was sold in auction at a shockingly low price collusively and fraudulently and the Executing Court which is the best Judge of its own proceedings having unearthed the collusion by the auction purchaser in submitting the bid rightly passed the order setting aside auction sale under its inherent power under section 57 of the Ain, 2003. He has further submitted that the High Court Division travelled beyond its jurisdiction in passing the impugned judgment and order in as much as it also set aside "the subsequent orders relating to setting aside the auction sale" passed by the Executing Court, though the writ petition was filed challenging Order No. XL dated 29-7-2008 and the Rule Nisi was issued accordingly and, as such, the impugned judgment and order calls for interference by this Court by giving leave. 

 11. Mr Siddique has referred to the photostat copies of the two firisty forms filed with the additional paper book on behalf of the petitioner to show that the auction purchaser already received the 3(three) pay orders dated 21-5-2008, 6-8-2008 and 27-8-2008 for the sum of Taka 6,65,500, 6,65,000 and 3,13,000 respectively deposited by the judgment-debtor by making endorsement on the body of those firisty forms, so he could not maintain the writ petition, but these facts could not be brought to the notice of the High Court Division at the time of hearing the writ petition and could not also be brought on record while filing the leave petition. Mr Siddique has lastly submitted that if this Court finds that the application filed before the Executing Court under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was not maintain- able, this Court in exercise of its power vested in it under article 104 of the Constitution to do complete justice, can very much take notice of the facts considered by the Executing Court and the subsequent developments that took place during the pendency of the writ petition and dispose of the leave petition finally since the auction purchaser is very much present before this Court and the plaintiff-Bank had already filed application in the Artha Jari Case that it had no dues from the judgment-debtor and it would not proceed with the Artha Jari Case and accordingly, the Executing Court allowed the prayer disposing of the case. ln support of his contention, he has referred the case of M/s Gannysons Limited vs Sonali Bank, 37DLR (AD) 42. 

 12. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of the auction purchaser- respondent, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He has submitted that since the judgment-debtor failed to apply for setting aside of the auction sale by making necessary deposit under the appropriate provision of the Code, he was not entitled to get the sale set aside, particularly, in view of the fact that the bainama was registered and the sale certificate was given to the auction purchaser. Mr Islam has submitted that the High Court Division took the correct view that in view of the specific provision in the Code, the application filed by the judgment-debtor under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was not maintainable in law Mr Islam has vehemently opposed the submission of Mr Siddique on the point that the auction purchaser received the auction purchased money along with the other amounts deposited by the judgment-debtor pursuant to the order of the Executing Court impugned in the writ petition by accepting the pay orders making endorsement on the firisty forms. He has submitted that such a procedure is unknown in civil jurisdiction and the firisty forms filed with the additional paper book showing such endorsement are nothing but the act of forgery. He has submitted that admittedly, the pay orders in respect of Taka 16,43,000 were deposited in the name of the Executing Court, so those could be paid back to the auction purchaser only by an order of the Executing Court on the application filed by the auction purchaser. Mr Islam by referring to the order sheets of the Artha Jari Case has showed that neither any such application was filed by the auction purchaser nor any order was passed by the Executing Court in that respect. He has categorically stated that the auction purchaser did not receive the auction purchased money allegedly deposited by the judgment-debtor through pay orders and the signatures appearing on the two firisty forms are not signatures of the auction purchaser. He has also relied upon the statements in that regard made in the application filed on behalf of the auction purchaser to reject the additional paper book filed on behalf of the judgment-debtor in which photostat copies of the 2(two) firisty forms have been filed. 

 13. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division, in fact, made the Rule Nisi absolute on the finding that in view of section 26 of the Ain,2003, the provisions of rules89 and 90 of Order XXI of the Code were applicable, but the judgment-debtor without filing application under any of the said rules filed the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale, the same was not maintainable. The High Court Division further found that at the time of filing the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003, the judgment-debtor instead of depositing the amount as specified in the proclamation of sale, deposited only the amount on which the mortgaged property was sold in auction and 10% compensation on the bid money. Therefore, the judgment-debtor did not comply with the provisions of Order XXI, rule 89 of the Code which provides that at the time of filing such application the amount specified in the proclamation of sale for the recovery of which “sale was ordered for payment to the decree-holder and a sum equivalent of 5% of the purchase money for payment to the purchaser has to be deposited.”  The High Court Division further observed that the judgment-debtor claimed that he was in Korea and in his absence, the decree was obtained in the suit by practising fraud, but he failed to produce before the Court an iota of evidence to 'show that he informed the Bank about his departure for Korea or about his address in Korea so that the Bank could know about his address in Korea and could communicate with him. The High Court Division further held that mere assertion that "the judgment and decree was obtained by fraud" was not enough, it must be shown that the Bank was aware of the fact that the judgment-debtor left for foreign country (South Korea) and it was informed about his last address, otherwise the provision of service of summons/ notice under sections 7 and J06f the Ain, 2003 and the execution case respectively would be meaning- less and nugatory. The High Court Division further held that if a defendant/judgment-debtor leaves for a foreign country the notice/summons is to be served at his last known address but the Executing Court did not consider "this legal aspect" of the case. The High Court Division further observed that an application could be filed also under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code on the ground of material irregularity or fraud, "if there has been any material irregularity or fraud in the auction sale of processes", but no such application was filed as well. The High Court Division lastly found that inherent power as stipulated in section 57 of the Ain, 2003 is subject to the provision of the Ami 2003, power under that section could be exercised, had there been no provisions in the Code for setting aside the sale and again if the application was filed under Order XXI, rules 89/90, then those could be registered as miscellaneous case and decide on taking evidence and the Executing Court was not empowered to set aside the auction sale after its confirmation and registration of the Bainama. 

 15. From the affidavit-of-compliance filed by the judgment-debtor before the High Court Division, it appears that the judgment-debtor specifically stated therein that as per the verbal order of the Court, he deposited the entire dues of the Bank amounting to Taka 36,35,550 vide two receipts dated 26-1-2011 and 31-1-2011. Though the High Court Division in its judgment observed that no such order was passed, it merely "asked the parties if amicable settlement is possible", but the parties failed, yet fact remains that the judgment-debtor paid the entire dues of the Bank as borne out from the application filed by the plaintiff-Bank in the Artha Jari Case, on 1-8-2011 wherein it admitted the said fact (the application has been filed with the additional paper book filed by the auction purchaser) and also from the certificate issued by the Assistant General Manager of the plaintiff- Bank on 20-7-2011 (the certificate has been filed with the additional paper book filed by the judgment-debtor). With the affidavit of compliance photostat copies of the two receipts showing the payment of the said amount to the Bank were annexed as annexure- ‘4(1)’ and ‘4(2)’. Besides depositing the entire dues of the Bank, the judgment-debtor also deposited Taka 16,43,000 pursuant to the impugned order dated 29-7-2008, this amount included Taka 3 63 000 being the amount of interest from 7-8-2005 (the date of auction sale) to 7-8-2008 on the bid money of Taka 12,10,000 and other costs of Taka 70,000. Although the auction purchaser filed an application before this Court under the caption: "An application for rejecting the additional paper book" these facts of deposit by the judgment-debtor have not been denied. With the application for rejection of the additional paper book filed by the auction purchaser writ-petitioner, the entire order sheets of the Artha Jari Case have been annexed. From Order No. XLV dated 12-9-2011 (this order has also been filed with additional paper book filed by the judgment-debtor), it also prima facie appears that on behalf of the decree-holder-Bank, an application was filed in the Artha Jari case on 1-8-2011 making the prayer to withdraw the case on the ground that since the entire decretal dues was paid to the Bank by the judgment- debtor, it would not proceed the case and accordingly, the Executing Court by its order of the said date disposed of the execution case with the full satisfaction. 

 16. Before the Executing Court, the judgment-debtor categorically stated that the value of the auction sold land was Taka 40,00,000. Before this Court in the affidavit-in-reply, it has been specifically stated that the mortgaged land was sold in auction at Taka 12,10,000 which was shockingly low. It further appears that the judgment-debtor took loan of Taka 16,14,000 on 13-4-1995 by mortgaging the auction sold land and the Executing Court in the impugned order clearly stated that the sale of the auction sold land (in the order wrongly written as the suit land) on 7-8-2005, i.e. after 10 years at Taka 12,10,2000 "was definitely not a market price." The Executing Court also believed the judgment-debtor's case that there is a homestead in the auction sold land and except that land he has no land to live in. 

 18. Whether there is any homestead in the auction sold land is basically a question of fact. From the impugned order of the Executing Court, it appears that it took notice of the said fact as claimed by the judgment-debtor. The High Court Division in its judgment has not said anything whether there is any homestead in the auction sold land or not. The High Court Division has not also said anything as to the place of the judgment-debtor's permanent residence. But the Executing Court, as it appears from the impugned order, believed the assertion of the judgment-debtor made in the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 that there IS a homestead on the auction sold land, and except that land, he has no other land to live in. The judgment-debtor made the same assertion in the affidavit-in-opposition and in the affidavit-in-reply filed in the writ petition. Furthermore, it is very difficult to come to any conclusion as to whether there is any homestead on the auction sold land or not relying on the photograph of the auction sold land allegedly taken by the auction purchaser as submitted by Mr Islam. Mentioning of an address in a passport as permanent address does not disprove the assertion of the judgment-debtor made on oath before the High Court Division that there is a homestead in the auction sold land and he has been living there along with his family members. It further appears from the affidavit-in-reply submit- ted by the judgment-debtor that he categorically stated therein that he was in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006 as evident from his passport, the ex-parte decree was obtained fraudulently on 9-8-2004 and the auction sale was held on 7-8-2005. In support of the said statements the judgment-debtor filed the photostat copy of the relevant pages of the passport before the High Court Division and we have also perused the same; the passport clearly supports the claim of the judgment-debtor that he was in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006. The fact, that the judgment- debtor was in South Korea during the said period, has not been denied either by the auction purchaser or by the decree holder-Bank, thus it is clear that the ex-parte decree and the auction sale was passed and held respectively during the absence of the judgment-debtor. It is also a fact that as back as on 29-7-2008 (the impugned order challenged in the writ petition) the Executing Court, in order to compensate the auction purchaser, directed the judgment-debtor to pay Taka 3,63,00,000 as 10% interest on the bid money from the date of auction sale, i.e. on 7-8-2005 to 7-8-2008 and also a cost of Taka 70,000 which the judgment-debtor deposited within 30 days from the date of the said order as evident from Order No. XLI dated 28-8-2008 of the Artha Jari Case. Therefore, it appears to us that the auction purchaser was duly compensated, but he, without accepting the said money, filed the writ petition and fought it and ultimately won through the impugned judgment and order. It will not be out of context to state' that although the sale certificate was issued and the Bainama was registered, the auction purchaser was not put into the possession of the auction soldland and it is the judgment-debtor who is in possession thereof. 

 21, The Executing Court also considered the fact that during the relevant time, the judgment- debtor was in South Korea and came to the finding that "From the copy of the passport it appears that during this whole period the petitioner was in South Korea and, as such, ends of justice would be best meet (sic) if the auction sale is set-aside." We do not find this conclusion of the Executing Court without any basis, because the relevant pages of the passport of ,the judgment-debtor substantiates that he had been in South Korea from before January, 2003 to August, 2006, whereas the ex-parte decree was passed on 9-8-2004 and the auction sale was held on 7-8-2005. The Executing Court also gave finding that there was-material irregularity in conducting the sale which caused substantial injury to the applicant (the judgment-debtor) and such injury was the result of fraud. But while making the Rule Nisi absolute, the High Court Division did not at all consider these factual aspects if the case, and, in fact, it set aside the orders of the Executing Court only on technical point that in view of the specific provisions of the Code in Order XXI, rule 89, the application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 was not maintainable in law. 

 22. Be that as it may; considering the facts and circumstances of the case. and the findings of the Executing Court, as discussed hereinbefore, particularly, the following; 

 (g) the judgment-debtor, besides depositing Taka 16,43,000 also paid the entire dues of the Bank amounting to Taka 36,35,550 during the pendency of the writ petition. The decree-holder-Bank duly received the money deposited by the judgment-debtor and filed application in the Artha Jari Case on 1-8-2011 for disposal of the case as being withdrawn, stating specifically that it had no dues due to the judgment-debtor, the Executing Court accordingly, allowed the prayer by its order dated 12-9-2011. 

 23. We are of the view that this is a fit case to exercise the power conferred upon this Court under article 104 of the Constitution to do complete justice. In this regard, we may refer the case of M/s Gannysons Ltd and another (supra) as relied upon by Mr Siddique. In that case, this Court exercised the power under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice on the following facts: 

 "Sonali Bank, respondent No.1, obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 for foreclosure and sale of the mortgaged properties belonging to the appellant company and put it into execution in Title Execution No. 46 of 1980. Appellant-company appeared before the Court and prayed for staying the execution of the decree on the grounds that since the Bank proceeded against the appellant Company's properties being treated as abandoned by the Government, the Directors of the appellant Company were not properly served with notice and that had, therefore, no knowledge of the aforesaid title suit. As a result they did not appear in the suit. Also the Government which was made a party did not take any steps. However, on the prayer of the appellant Company the proceeding in the execution case was stayed till 20-10-1981. In Writ Petition No. 720 of 1981 a Rule was issued at the instance of the appellant company on October 20, 1981. But it abated on 24-3-1982 after the proclamation of Martial Law. In Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 which was filed by the appellant Company under section 47 of the Code its prayer against the execution of the decree obtained in-Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 was disallowed by the Court. The appellant Company's appeal against this order was dismissed by the High Court Division on 9 November 1982. The appellant Company, being aggrieved, moved this Court, and, succeeded in having the appeal(Civil Appeal No. 43 of 1983) against the order of the trial Court rejecting their objection under section 47of the Code allowed. Appellants filed review petition against the judgment passed in the civil appeal against the concluding paragraph of the judgment which was as follows: 

 "Decree dated 27-3-1980 passed by the Subordinate Judge,3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 be stayed for six months and the Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 pending in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka be struck down." 

 "For that consistently with the reasoning's in the main body of the judgment and the decision allowing the appeal (CA No. 43 of 1983) arising out of Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 started under section 47CPC (at the instance of M/s Gannysons Ltd.) the Title Execution, Case No. 46 of 1980 pending in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, needs to be struck down and the said Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 of the same court allowed and that the order staying the decree dated 27-3-1980 in Title Suit No. 279 of 1976 of the 3rd Court of the Subordinate 'Judge needs to be deleted." 

 25. Considering the definition of abandoned property as given in President's Order No. XVI of 1972, it was found that  Gannysons Limited Company, in no circumstances, could be declared as an abandoned property, allowed the review application, declared that the property was not an abandoned property, struck down the execution case subject to payment of the decretal amount to, the Bank directly by the appellants and directed the Government to release the property treating Title Suit No. 508 of 1982 filed by the appellant as withdrawn being infructuous. In that case, Fazle Munim, CJ observed: 

 "17. In view of the circumstances above and in virtue of the power conferred upon this Court by the Constitution of Bangladesh, vide Article 104, to do complete justice in a case it is declared that Gannysons Limited is not an abandoned property, it should, therefore, be immediately, released. Along with the release of Gannysons Limited any of its properties, assets and capital should also be released and returned to it." 

 26. Since we are exercising the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice, we are riot at all required to enter into the legal question as to the maintainability of the application filed by the judgment-debtor in the Artha Jari Case under section 57 of the Ain, 2003. The question may be decided in an appropriate case if occasion arises. 

 (a) The order dated 29-7-2008 (impugned in the writ petition) passed by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Artha Jari Case No. 52 of 2004 is maintained, the judgment and order dated 14-2-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4 of 2009 is set- aside. 

 (b) The Joint District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur is directed to pass necessary order/ orders in Artha Jari Case No. 52 of 2004 (though the same was disposed of by Order No. XLV dated 12-9-2011) so that the auction purchaser, namely, Md Asaduzzaman Belal can withdraw/receive Taka 16,43,000 (Sixteen Lakhs Forty Three Thousand) deposited by the judgment-debtor pursuant to the order dated 29-7-2008, passed in the case, if not withdrawn in the meantime.
